title: Bookings tab — accepting requests, calendar, cancellation
body:
On the **„Foglalások”** (Bookings) tab you answer your guests' booking requests, and you also see your calendar here.
If a request is waiting for your decision, a small number (badge) next to the tab name shows how many requests are waiting. The number
stays until you have decided — it does not disappear when you open the tab.

At the top of the **„Áttekintés”** (Overview) page a bar also appears, showing how many requests are waiting for your
decision and how soon the most urgent one expires. Under **„Teendők”** (To-dos) every waiting
request gets its own row: the **„Döntök”** (Decide) button takes you straight to that request, and for a price-quote request
the **„Ajánlatot küldök”** (Send an offer) button takes you to the offer page.

![Screenshot: the Bookings tab on a phone, with waiting requests](assets/hu/screen.png)

**In the free trial, without online booking:** if the trial package does not include online booking, the tab says so
(**„Az online foglalás nincs benne a próba csomagjában”** — online booking is not included in the trial package). Your guests' enquiries are then shown by the
**„Érdeklődések az Üzenetekben”** (Enquiries in Messages) button; you can add the booking calendar with the **„Megrendelem — csomag és
modulok”** (Order — package and modules) button.

## A booking request has arrived — what should I do?

The **„Döntésre váró kérések”** (Requests awaiting decision) section is at the top of the tab — on a phone even the calendar only comes
below it, so that the decision buttons are on screen without scrolling. You see the requests ordered by
**response deadline**: the one expiring sooner is on top — even if it arrived
later. (This sentence is also shown above the list.) Every request shows the guest's name, the
dates, the number of guests (with children: *3 guests, of whom 1 child*), the room (for a multi-room request
all requested rooms, separated by commas), the guest's message, and a badge showing how much time is left:
**„Ma lejár”** (Expires today), **„Holnap lejár”** (Expires tomorrow) or **„Van még idő”** (There is still time) — urgent ones are also marked by a red
stripe on the left edge of the card.

If a request is for more guests than the room's capacity — for several rooms, the sum of the requested rooms'
capacities — (this can only happen with an older request, or if you reduced the capacity
afterwards), a red warning appears on the card and in the **„Visszaigazolom”** (Confirm) step
as well: *"Note: the guest is requesting for 7 people, the capacity is 4."* The same appears at the top of the notification
email and on the confirmation page opened from the email.

If meals can be chosen at your property (breakfast, half board — you set this in the Prices, seasons
module), a label on the card shows what the guest asked for. Tapping the **„Az ár
tételesen”** (Itemised price) row opens it up to show how the total is made up: nights, meals, child supplement
— as the guest saw it when sending the request. If you change the prices later, this does not change on a request
that has already arrived.

If you would like to talk to the guest first, the **„Felhívom”** (Call) button lets you call with one tap (your phone's
dialler opens), and the **„Írok neki”** (Write to them) button lets you write an email. The link at the bottom of the card opens the calendar
on the month and room the guest is asking for — so you can see what is around it.

You choose between two options:

- **„Visszaigazolom”** (Confirm) — the confirmation opens inside the card, at full width. The question
  names the guest, below it the dates, the room and the amount, and what will happen. You can also write
  a message to the guest (optional, e.g. "When you arrive, please ring at the green gate."): tap the
  **„+ Üzenetet írok a vendégnek”** (+ Write a message to the guest) label. With the **„Igen, visszaigazolom”** (Yes, confirm) button the days
  become booked, and the guest receives an email with your message and a calendar attachment, with which
  they can add the trip to their phone's calendar in one tap. With the **„Mégsem”** (Cancel) button nothing happens,
  and the request stays where it was.
- **„Elutasítom”** (Decline) — asks in the same way. You can also give a reason (**„+ Megírom, miért (nem kötelező)”** (+ I'll write why (optional))
  — the guest will read this); you send it with the **„Igen, elutasítom”** (Yes, decline) button, and the days stay
  free. Here too there is **„Mégsem”** (Cancel). If you write why, the guest's email says that you cannot
  host them this time and quotes your reason (for example: there would be too many people). Without a reason the email
  says that the requested dates are not available.

While the confirmation is open, the button for the opposite decision is hidden — so you cannot
tap it by accident.

## Multi-room request — all or none

On the website a guest can request several rooms in one request, even all of them (someone who wants the whole house
selects every room). You recognise such a request like this:

- the badge next to the guest's name also shows the number of rooms, for example "Booking request · 2 rooms"
  (for a request without a price "Price-quote request · 2 rooms");
- the card lists the requested rooms separated by commas;
- next to the **„Visszaigazolom”** (Confirm) button the number of rooms is shown in brackets, for example "(2 rooms)", and the
  confirmation states that the days of all requested rooms will become booked — towards the connected
  portals as well.

The decision applies to **the whole request**: either you confirm all requested rooms, or you decline the whole
request. You cannot accept individual rooms separately — if you could only offer some of the rooms, write to the
guest (**„Írok neki”** (Write to them)) and ask them to send a new request for those. The total is in the top
row of the card; if you tap the **„Az ár tételesen”** (Itemised price) row, the breakdown by room opens
(this only exists for requests with a price — for a price-quote request you set the price).

You can also make the same decision from the email you received about the request, without logging in: below the email's
**„Foglalások megnyitása”** (Open bookings) button, in the **„Gyors döntés innen is:”** (Quick decision from here too:) row, tapping the **„Elfogadom”** (Accept) or
**„Nem szabad”** (Not available) link opens a confirmation page with the request details (guest, period,
and the price, if there is one), and there you decide with the **„Igen, elfogadom”** (Yes, accept) or **„Igen, elutasítom”** (Yes, decline) button.
Until you press it, nothing changes — so your email program's link checker cannot decide
for you either. (For a price-quote request the first link is **„Ajánlatot küldök”** (Send an offer): it opens the offer page.) On the **„Üzenetek”** (Messages)
tab, at the top of the opened message, the **„Foglalások megnyitása”** (Open bookings) button takes you straight to this request;
below it the **„Gyors döntés innen is:”** (Quick decision from here too:) buttons ask first (with the guest's name), and there
is a **„Mégsem”** (Cancel) there too. In the email the guest's phone number can also be tapped.
If you do not reply within the set time, the request expires and the guest receives a polite notification.

## A price-quote request has arrived — the guest did not see a price

If the guest chooses a room or period for which your price list has no price, the page does not
promise them a booking but asks for a price quote. On such a request you read: **„A vendég nem látott
árat — árajánlatot kért. Adja meg az árat, és a rendszer elküldi neki.”** (The guest did not see a price — they asked for a quote. Enter the price and the system will send it to them.) There is no
"Confirm" button here, because it would finalise the booking without a price. You have two options: if you cannot
host them, the **„Elutasítom”** (Decline) button works the same as usual. If you would host them, send
an offer:

1. Tap the **„Ajánlatot küldök”** (Send an offer) button (the same button is also in the email you received about the request,
   without logging in). The offer page opens.
2. The page lists the requested nights. Nights for which you already have a price (for example the high season) are fixed at the existing
   price. You only need to enter a price for the missing nights in the **„Ár éjszakánként”** (Price per night) field —
   the amount is calculated immediately below it. If the guest also asked for meals (for example breakfast), that
   appears on a separate row ("requested by the guest — the set meal supplement"), and the **„Összesen”** (Total) already
   includes it.
3. You can write a message to the guest (for example "We'll gladly set up the cot.").
4. By default the price applies **only to this request**: your price list does not change, and where you have no price,
   guests on the website will still ask for a quote. If you also want to add the price to the price list,
   tick the **„Mentsem az árlistába is?”** (Save it to the price list too?) box and choose:
   - **„Csak a kért napokra”** (Only for the requested days) — the price goes into the price list only for these nights; for these
     days the property becomes bookable on the website without a quote request, for other days guests still
     ask for a quote. After the last night of the stay the price is removed from the price list.
   - **„Alapárként”** (As base price) — without dates, until the next change: valid for every night
     that has no seasonal price. This makes the room (or, if you only rent it as a whole, the whole house) **bookable**
     on the website — from then on guests can send a booking request without a quote request, which you
     confirm.

   The framed sentence below the choice always states what the consequence of your choice will be.

   **For a multi-room price-quote request** (if one of the requested rooms has no price) the rooms priced in the price list
   are listed on the page with their own prices, itemised — you do not need to touch these. You only enter a single
   price per night for the rooms without a price, together: the field label is then "Price per night:"
   and the room's name (for several rooms without a price "Price per night, together:" and their names). If none of the requested
   rooms has a price, or you price per person, the label is "Price per night, for the … rooms together", and the
   price applies to all requested rooms. This price applies only to this request and cannot go into the price list, so
   the **„Mentsem az árlistába is?”** (Save it to the price list too?) box does not appear here at all.
5. Tap the **„Ajánlat küldése”** (Send offer) button. If you cannot host them after all, you can decline here with the
   **„Nem szabad”** (Not available) button.

![Screenshot: the price section of the offer page on a phone, with a price entered, the "Save it to the price list too?" box and the "Only for this request." sentence](assets/hu/offer.png)

After sending, the page confirms in a green box how much was sent, and also whether the price went into the
price list; the **„Foglalások megnyitása”** (Open bookings) button brings you back here, to the "Sent offers" list.

The guest receives the offer by email and can accept it with one button. **The offer is not yet a
booking:** the days stay free until the guest accepts it. If someone else books them in the meantime
and the guest then tries to accept the offer, the page tells them that the days are
taken, and you receive a notification. If the time set in the **„Ennyi idő után magától lejár a kérés”** (The request expires automatically after this time) field
in the Modules → Online booking settings runs out, the
offer expires — both you and the guest receive a notification. (If it is set to 0, the offer does not expire.)
If the guest declines the offer, we let you know by email, and the days stay free.

Offers awaiting a reply are shown in the **„Ajánlatra vár”** (Awaiting offer reply) section, with their expiry time. If the guest
says they accept not with the email's button but by phone or in a reply email, tap the
**„A vendég elfogadta (telefonon / levélben)”** (The guest accepted (by phone / by email)) button — the same happens as if they had pressed
it: the days become booked, and the guest receives the confirmation with the price.

At the bottom of the Bookings tab the **„Kiküldött ajánlatok”** (Sent offers) list shows every offer you have sent
from the system — including those that are already closed: to whom, for what, for how much (with the price per night below the
amount), when it was sent,
what became of it (for example "Accepted — booking", "Declined", "Expired — no reply", "Taken in the meantime"),
and in the **„Árlista”** (Price list) column (on a phone, in the card's "Price list:" row) whether the price went into the
price list. Above the list you can filter:
**„Mind”** (All), **„Válaszra vár”** (Awaiting reply), **„Elfogadta”** (Accepted), **„Nem lett belőle”** (Did not happen).

A price saved for the requested days appears on the Modules tab, in the "Prices, seasons" module, as an **„Alapár, dátummal”** (Base price, with dates)
row, together with the dates; you can also delete it there.

## If several guests request the same period

If a request's days overlap another request (for a multi-room request: on any of the requested rooms), a
red marker on the request warns you. The
**„Visszaigazolom”** (Confirm) button then opens a selection window: on the calendar you see in colour who
requests which nights, and you can choose whom to give the period to. The **„Visszaigazolom — a
többit elutasítom”** (Confirm — decline the others) button, after confirmation, sends a confirmation to the chosen guest and
automatically declines the other overlapping requests — those guests also receive an email
saying that the requested room is already booked for this period. At a property with several rooms only the request
for the same room is declined: a request for a different room remains, and you decide
on it separately. The window shows next to each request which room it is for.

## The calendar

The **„Naptár”** (Calendar) bar (on a phone below the requests awaiting decision, on a computer on the left) summarises the month
in one row when collapsed; tapping it opens it. It opens by itself on the month and room where your
next decision is: the most urgent request — or, if none is waiting, the next arrival.

- **Day with a dashed border:** a guest is requesting this night, but it is **not booked** yet — according to
  the legend **„kért éjszaka — döntésre vár, még NEM foglalt”** (requested night — awaiting decision, NOT yet booked). Tapping it takes you to
  the request, where you can decide.
- Tapping a **free day** blocks it manually (guests see it as booked); tapping again unblocks it.
- Tapping a **green (guest booking) day** opens the booking: you see the guest's details, and with the
  **„Foglalás lemondása”** (Cancel booking) button you can also cancel it. The button does not cancel immediately: a confirmation window
  opens titled **„Biztosan lemondja ezt a foglalást?”** (Are you sure you want to cancel this booking?), with the guest's name and the period, below it
  the **„Rövid indoklás a vendégnek küldött levélbe (nem kötelező)”** (Short reason for the email sent to the guest (optional)) field. With the **„Lemondom a
  foglalást”** (Cancel the booking) button the days are freed and the guest receives a cancellation email with the reason; with the
  **„Mégsem — megtartom”** (No — keep it) button everything stays as it was. The cancellation cannot be undone.
- **Striped day:** that day is held by **another room** of the property (for example a booking that arrived earlier for the
  whole house also books the rooms). A multi-room booking is not striped:
  it appears as its own guest booking in the calendar of each requested room. This day **cannot be tapped** — it can
  neither be unblocked nor opened here. The day is freed by the room that holds it.

## The summary tiles

The three tiles (**„Döntésre vár”** (Awaiting decision), **„Következő érkezés”** (Next arrival), **„Idén visszaigazolt”** (Confirmed this year)) open
when tapped: the list of waiting requests jumps to the request, the arrivals list opens the
booking in the calendar.

## Earlier requests and cancellation

The **„Korábbi kérések”** (Earlier requests) list shows every decided request together with the decision. You can cancel a confirmed
booking with the **„Lemondom”** (Cancel) link (you can also give a reason — the guest receives it by email).
When a multi-room booking is cancelled, the days of all its rooms are freed together.
The guest can also cancel themselves using the link in their confirmation email — in that case you receive an email, and the
days are freed automatically.

**Who wrote it? — the row tells you.** Several messages can collect under one request, so each
quote box names its author: **„Vendég”** (Guest — what they wrote when booking; their question stays
there even after you have decided), **„Ön”** (You — what you sent when confirming or declining),
**„Rendszer”** (System — what the system wrote, for example on expiry) and **„Megjegyzés”** (Note — your own note,
only for you). So you do not have to remember whose words you are reading. A message you wrote with a
price offer is also labelled **„Ön”** (You), even if in the end the guest accepted the offer.

## Where do the notifications go?

We send emails about requests to the address set in Modules → Booking settings — you can enter several
addresses separated by commas (e.g. reception and owner). If no address is set, they go to your
account's email address.

## Striped days in the calendar

A striped day means that **another room** of the property holds that night: either a (former) booking applies to
the whole house, or — if you are looking at the whole house's calendar because you only rent it as a whole
— one of its rooms is booked.
These days cannot be tapped here; in the Modules → Online booking calendar, tap the day to see
which room holds it and who.
